correctness.rationale: The descending link of an inserted vertex in the unfilled graph is a discrete earlier-neighbor set; strong pairings occur exactly at one earlier neighbor. Once vertices from three different multipartite parts have appeared, all future vertices have >=2 earlier neighbors and cannot pair. In the initial complete bipartite section, a count according to first and second occurrences of the parts bounds the number of pairs by the largest involved part. Strictly unique largest C enforces n as maximal size and yields exactly F_r and F_{r,c} for r outside C and c in C; exhibited orders realize all. For fixed r the base simplex on y_{r,c} plus n independent facets with new flap x_{r,c} is connected and collapsible; vertex sets for different r are disjoint. Barycentrically retract each flap and base simplex equivariantly to r. Face count follows by disjoint base/flap enumeration and pure disconnectedness (s>=2,n>=2) prevents shellability. Independent small exact vertex-order enumeration confirmed facet lists for (1,1,2),(1,1,3),(2,1,3),(1,2,4).
